messages.content: hey report that the baby has been producing excessive frothy saliva since birth and experiences episodes of coughing, cyanosis, why th efrothy saliva?

The baby can't swallow. The esophagus ends in a blind pouch. **Frothy saliva accumulates because it has nowhere to go** — it pools in the proximal pouch and spills over into the trachea. That's also why you see **coughing and cyanosis with feeding**: milk goes down, hits the blind pouch, then refluxes into the airway. The froth is just **saliva mixed with air from repeated swallowing attempts** — a mechanical consequence of a disconnected foregut. Contrast with a TEF without atresia: those babies get recurrent pneumonia, not frothy saliva from birth. At the bedside, **pass an NG tube — it should coil in the pouch and not reach the stomach**, confirming the diagnosis.
producing excessive frothy saliva since birth and experiences episodes of coughing, cyanosis, and regurgitation immediately after attempts at breastfeeding - this is it!

That's the classic triad. **Esophageal atresia with distal tracheoesophageal fistula** — the proximal pouch ends blindly, so saliva pools and overflows into the airway. The distal fistula connects the trachea to the stomach, so **air goes down into the GI tract, and gastric acid can reflux up into the lungs**. That's why you get **coughing and cyanosis immediately with feeds** — the milk hits the blind pouch, can't pass, and spills over. The **frothy saliva is the giveaway** — it's been present since birth, not just with feeding. At the bedside, **coiling of an NG tube in the proximal pouch on a plain film** seals it. No other diagnosis explains all three findings from day one.
